newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan port workers still undecided on night shifts.
newsitem.headline: Japan port workers still undecided on night shifts.

text.p: Leading Japanese port workers' unions have not yet decided whether to resume night shifts after failing so far to reach an agreement with management on wage negotiations, a union official said on Wednesday.
"There will be no night work," an official with the Council of Dock Workers' Union of Tokyo said.
Night shift workers at Japan's major ports, including Yokohama, Osaka, Tokyo, Kobe, Nagoya and Kanmon, have refused to handle freight from 6 p.m. to 8 a.m. (0900 GMT to 2300 GMT) since March 31.

The union official said that a few fringe labour unions had reached an agreement with management on wages, but that many of the unions directly involved with handling night freight were still negotiating with management.
"There has been no decision to resume night work at the six leading ports," he said.
